extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, researchers, and professional readers interested in book/monograph evaluations across biology, anthropology, engineering, and chemistry)
extracted.subtask_description: Extract standards and evaluative criteria used in scholarly book reviews (natural history, anthropology, engineering, chemistry, etc.) in a scientific journal. Focuses on what makes a good scientific monograph or technical book and common defects noted by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomic and empirical thoroughness
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions should be based upon an exhaustive examination of numerous specimens and the author’s unique knowledge of the organisms in their native haunts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine careful comparison of many types with field observations; draw on specimens in various stages of plumage and distribution data to support taxonomic decisions. Anti-pattern: basing taxonomic changes on limited material or superficial comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear separation of wild versus acclimatised/crossed forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw a sharp line of demarcation between forms as they exist in their real zone of distribution and forms which have been crossed indiscriminately and acclimatised in all parts of the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat introduced/hybrid populations separately from natural wild populations when assessing species/subspecies status. Failure to separate these can lead to inflated numbers of described forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent application of genus criteria (geographic non-overlap)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply genus-level criteria consistently — e.g., the author’s stated criterion that genera should be geographically non-overlapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and use a clear criterion for higher-level taxonomy and apply it across the group. Inconsistency in criteria undermines classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple lines of evidence for classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification decisions should rest on diverse observations (e.g., intensive local collecting showing mixed sub‑species in a covey, plus evidence from semi-wild hybrids introduced elsewhere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine field collecting, hybridization/introgression data, morphology, distribution and ecological information. Single lines of evidence are weaker than concordant multiple lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution mapping and environmental context
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide maps delineating distributions and discuss environment and barriers as part of taxonomic treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps are a very useful adjunct to illustrate ranges; include habitat descriptions and geographic barriers that explain distributional patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and suitability of illustrations and plates
rubrics_metrics.description: Include careful reproductions and photogravure plates depicting principal forms, haunts, and nests; illustrations should add to the attractiveness and scientific utility of the volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality plates from capable artists are important; poor reproduction quality relative to preceding volumes is a defect. Photographs by the author add value when clear and well-chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate fieldwork duration and language competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Field studies intended to characterise peoples or organisms should have adequate duration and, for ethnographic work, the investigator should know the language or rely minimally on interpreters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short residencies and heavy dependence on interpreters reduce reliability of conclusions; long-term residence (decades) and language fluency strengthen claims. Anti-pattern: claiming deep cultural/language insights after a brief stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of transcription and notational conventions suitable to the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt established transcription systems familiar to the book’s primary readership (e.g., English readers) rather than unfamiliar foreign alphabets, unless clearly justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Switching to a less familiar alphabet can confuse readers and misrepresent sounds; diacritical marks strange to the audience are undesirable. Ensure phonetic distinctions (e.g., vowel contrasts) are correctly recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with and acknowledgement of prior literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers expect authors to acknowledge predecessors and engage with existing bibliography rather than appropriating previous information without citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss where and why the work agrees or differs from predecessors; failing to credit prior laborious work or ignoring key references is a serious defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of evidence from interpretation; value of hypothesis formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide solid empirical evidence and, where interpretation/theory is proposed, make clear what is evidence and what is speculative; proposing theories is valuable if presented transparently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to propound theories (promotes research) but authors should not present tentative or speculative interpretations as established fact; explicitness about the evidential status of claims is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target-audience technical prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical works should state and match their assumed reader background — e.g., hydro-electric engineering requires sound training in civil, mechanical, and electrical engineering to appreciate fully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warn readers about prerequisites; do not oversimplify multi-disciplinary technical material for novices without guidance. Anti-pattern: presenting complex multidisciplinary engineering without noting required background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate treatment of hydrology and water-resource estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the relationship of available water to watershed rainfall, the power obtainable, flow measurement, and related hydrological principles adequately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These topics should receive central, thorough treatment in any hydro-electric engineering text; inadequate coverage weakens the book’s utility for design and planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive treatment of turbines including performance curves
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe turbine types, design principles, and behaviour under variable gate opening and speed, and provide characteristic and efficiency curves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include typical characteristic curves (unit power vs unit speed for gate openings) and efficiency curves under varying loads; discuss how to choose the most suitable turbine for particular site conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth on regulation and hydraulic transients (surge tanks, governor interactions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain speed regulation, hydraulic problems from sudden flow changes, theory of the surge tank, and dangers of period oscillation synchronising with governors; include relevant formulas/solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss Johnson’s approximate formula and differential surge tank solutions where relevant; point out synchronization hazards and practical remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest labeling of revision status and availability of indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims such as 'entirely rewritten' or 'entirely revised' should be accurate; essential production features like indexes must be present and appropriately placed (index confined to a later volume is a defect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mislabel minor updates as full rewrites; include a usable index in each volume or clearly indicate limitations to accessibility when indexing is deferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and selection for user utility
rubrics_metrics.description: For large reference works, prefer careful selection and pruning of material to avoid diffuse and indefinite sections and to keep the work crisp and usable for practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance encyclopedic completeness with usability; unnecessary verbosity or diffuse exposition frustrates experienced readers and reduces practical value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on practical analytical methods and public-health relevance (food/milk analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present standard methods of analysis, clear interpretation guidance, and highlight public-health relevant sections (cleanliness, bacterial contamination, tests like fermentation and direct dirt determination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include practical tests (fermentation test, direct dirt determination), discuss limitations of bacteriological detection for pathogens, and provide protocols for detecting adulteration (foreign fats) with interpretive notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability of principles versus ephemeral computational methods
rubrics_metrics.description: In technical predictive works (e.g., aeroplane performance), arithmetic methods may become obsolete, but underlying physical/design principles have greater permanence and are the lasting value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise conceptual framing and numerical assessment of contributions of separate items rather than relying solely on specific calculation techniques that may date quickly. Clarify scope (e.g., performance-focused works may not address safety).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical insider coverage of professional business practices
rubrics_metrics.description: For trade/business manuals (e.g., building contracts) include administration, office management, bookkeeping, trade memoranda, and candid descriptions of business methods used to obtain work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide practical, candid, and experience-based information valuable to practitioners and students; insider tips and frank discussion of methods are assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical clarity about speculative material (genetics/textbook claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not present speculative interpretations or unreplicated experimental claims as accepted doctrine; indicate where statements are tentative and require verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warn readers when interpretations are highly speculative; explicitly note that reports of mutations as a direct consequence of changed conditions require replication and ample confirmation before acceptance.
